**hooks.yaml `email:`** takes `to`, `subject` and either `template:` (emails/<name>.html, else the text itself) or an inline `body:`. Other keys are refused at write time.

**Reputation is shared.** Bounce/complaint events feed a per-app circuit breaker: complaint rate >0.5% or bounce rate >10% over 7 days auto-PAUSES the app's sending and emails the owner. Don't send to purchased/unverified lists - clean opt-in recipients only. The bounce rate counts hard bounces only, once per address (a temporary bounce such as a full mailbox does not count toward a pause); email status reports that number as hard_bounces_7d next to bounces_7d. A public form that mails an address the visitor types (sign-up confirmation, contact auto-reply) lets a stranger produce hard bounces on your sender, so rate-limit it (`rate_limit:` on the flow; sign-up is limited by the framework).

**A hard-bounce pause ends by itself; a complaint pause needs support.** The first hard-bounce pause lasts 24 hours, a second within 30 days of the last one 72 hours, and a third stays until support resumes it; a pause for spam complaints always stays until support resumes it. Email status (`benmore email <app>`, the dashboard Email tab, `email_domains` status) reports `paused`, `paused_reason` and, when the pause ends by itself, `paused_until` (RFC 3339); the owner's notice and the refused send say the same. Clean the recipient list before the pause ends.

**Rates are measured from the last resume.** When a pause ends, by itself or by support, the breaker starts counting again from that moment: the 20-send floor, the 10 hard-bounced addresses and the 3 complaints all apply to what happened since (sends from the day of the resume). A late bounce from mail sent before the pause does not pause the app again. A resume keeps event history and globally suppressed recipients.

**Suppression is platform-wide.** An address that hard-bounced or complained is refused for every app with a precise error - that's deliverability protection, not a bug. The suppression and deliverability checks read the recipient's address however it is written (`Name <addr>`, `<addr>`, a quoted local part), so a `to:` of `Jane Doe <jane@client.org>` is delivered and no spelling of a suppressed address gets through.
**Recipient cap per send: 50 across To, CC and BCC.** Batch bigger audiences across calls (and respect the daily quota).

**Copies.** Flow `with.cc` and `with.bcc` accept recipient-list text, with the same substitution rule as `to`: a request/row value is one mailbox unless explicitly marked `| recipients`. CC appears in the message headers; BCC is only in the SMTP/SES delivery envelope. Every address shares validation, suppression, deliverability and quota checks; a refused copy prevents the whole send. Control characters in address or header fields are rejected. hooks.yaml `email:` does not take `cc` or `bcc`.

**One recipient per `to:` value.** `to:` (flow `run: email` and hooks.yaml `email:`) lists several recipients only through commas written in the template (`to: "{{owner_email}}, ops@client.org"`), an env value (`{{env.ADMIN_EMAILS}}`), or a value marked as a list: `to: "{{ team_emails | recipients }}"` (in hooks.yaml write exactly `{{column | recipients}}`). Any other substituted value that contains a comma fails the send (`email to: … resolved to more than one address`) instead of mailing every address in it - a form's email field is data, and a visitor could otherwise put fifty addresses in it. To mail a dynamic list one message each, loop with `for_each`.
**The from-domain is enforced.** Tenants sending on the shared domain always send as <app-sub>@mail.benmore.ai regardless of EMAIL_FROM's local part; any other domain must be verified for THIS app.

**Unsubscribe.** A flow `run: email` step sets it from `with.unsubscribe_url` as the `List-Unsubscribe` header. The step accepts an absolute HTTPS URL and optional `unsubscribe_one_click: true` to add RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`. The flag defaults false and may be a template resolving exactly to true/false. One-click requires exactly one recipient across To, CC and BCC: each recipient needs their own message and URL so a copy cannot unsubscribe someone else. Opt in only when the URL carries a per-recipient token and accepts unauthenticated POST with body `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`; links opened by GET should require confirmation. An invalid/missing URL, fragment or userinfo fails an opted-in send. Put the token in the query or path so it reaches the POST handler. Without one-click, invalid dynamic URLs omit the optional header with a warning; invalid literal URLs are refused by the write gate. Keep a body unsubscribe link too.
**Self-hosted / OSS builds** have no platform service - configure SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS (AWS SES SMTP credentials work directly).

**Server log lines name a recipient by reference, not by address**: `EMAIL [...] to=addr#3f9c2a71b0de subject=...` and the SMS equivalents carry a keyed 12-hex-digit reference per recipient, stable within one deployment, so lines about one recipient can be matched to each other; the address or phone number itself is not in the log. To find what happened to one message, look for its subject and time, the provider message id on the sent line, or the flow/hook result.
